title: Wyjść czy przyjść?
title_en: Reading the front of the verb · out, to, up-to, back
note:
B2 Block 6a unit 2 (JAMES-LOCKED 2026-08-06, O7 overrule, locked decisions #1 and #2). A RECEPTIVE-ONLY reading lens on the core 4 spatial prefixes - wy- out, przy- to/arrive, do- reach/all-the-way, od- away/back. ZERO NEW LEMMAS: every single example is a verb or noun the course already taught, re-seen through the lens. teaches_lemmas is deliberately empty.

RECEPTIVE-ONLY IS IMPLEMENTED STRUCTURALLY, NOT BY PROMISE: type_items and use_items are EMPTY ARRAYS, on the live precedent of b1_virile_reco (B1-SPINE decision #1, 'RECOGNITION ONLY'), which ships the same way and audits clean. So the spine's requirement that 'the learner NEVER types a prefixed verb the course didn't teach' is met absolutely - there is no typing stage at all in this unit, and the question cannot arise. Tasks are recognition and discrimination only, exactly as the spine specifies: a 12-row meaning board and a quiz mixing frame-selection with straight comprehension items ('Doszedlem do apteki. - what happened?').

TITLE CORRECTED, and this is the one thing to check first. The planned tree label was 'Przedrostki · soczewka' / 'Prefixes · the reading lens'. check_new.py reports przedrostki, przedrostek AND soczewka all NEW - two untaught Polish words in learner-visible chrome, which the AGENTS title rule forbids outright ('Never put an untaught Polish form in a title', a rule its own text records being broken three times in one night). Retitled to the house pattern on the Ide czy jade? model, using two forms owned since b1_arrive_leave: 'Wyjsc czy przyjsc?'. The tree node's label/label_en were updated to match. The word przedrostek is still used, but only in body_pl, which AGENTS names as the one lane where untaught metalanguage is allowed by convention - the same lane b2_aspect_prefixes already uses it in.

HONESTY FENCES, all deliberate. (a) wypic is NOT a lens example and never appears: its wy- is completive, not spatial, and mixing it in would teach a false meaning - that verb is precisely b2_prefix_two_jobs's material, one unit later. Same exclusion for wydawac and wygrywac. (b) The opaque core-4 words the learner already owns - przyjaciel, przystanek, przychodnia, przyczyna, przyklad, odpowiedz, odpoczywac, odwiedzac - are excluded from the drilled stages ENTIRELY - not as examples and not as quiz distractors either, a distinction that mattered: przystanek and wycieczka were caught sitting as distractors in the przyjazd/odjazd item on a late self-check and swapped for pociag/autobus, because a przy-/wy- word standing in a lens item silently invites exactly the false reading this unit exists to prevent. The slide 1 caveat is written to cover them: the lens is a reading aid for verbs of coming and going, and Polish does not always cooperate. This is the locked line 'you can READ these; don't build new ones' made concrete rather than just asserted. (c) za-/po-/prze- get exactly one line naming them as making no promise, with no examples drilled, per locked decision #2. (d) No formation rule of any kind; no derivation is invited anywhere.

od- IS THE THIN ONE, logged: only two taught items carry a transparent od- (oddawac/oddaje from b1_giving, and the noun odjazd from a2_transport2). That is enough for an honest 3-row share of the board only because odjazd pairs against przyjazd, which makes the station-board contrast the natural payoff and gives od- a real everyday use rather than a single stranded verb. If James wants od- fuller, the material has to come from a later unit, not from inventing examples here.

HOMOGRAPH CHECK: ksiazki was drafted and REJECTED - a1_gen_ki teaches it as a GENITIVE singular, and 'oddaje ksiazki' would need the accusative plural; the item uses ksiazke instead, taught as an accusative by a1_miec. apteki is used only inside the taught chunk do apteki. Rejected as untaught: dlugo, wyjazd, wyjscie, pociagu, dworca, Warszawy.

intro.title: A tool for reading, not for building
intro.body:
You have met a lot of verbs now that are one verb with a small piece welded on the front: wyjść, przyjść, dojść, oddawać.

That front piece is often doing a job you can read. Once you know the four commonest ones, a verb you have never seen before will sometimes give you its meaning for free.

One warning, and it matters more than the lens itself: this is for READING. Do not build new verbs with it. Polish does not always cooperate — you already know przyjaciel (a friend) and przystanek (a bus stop), and neither of those is arriving anywhere. The lens is a reading aid for verbs of coming and going. Everything you SAY should stay a verb this course actually taught you.

intro.title: The four worth knowing
intro.body: Each one is shown here only on verbs you already own.

intro.title: Where you will actually see this
intro.body:
The clearest everyday payoff is a station board. You have known both of these words since A2 — now you can see why they are the pair they are.

przyjazd — przy- is the toward one, so this is the arrival.
odjazd — od- is the away one, so this is the departure.

Same word underneath; the front piece is the whole difference.

examples.en: I went out of the office.
I finally got all the way to the pharmacy.

intro.title: The ones that promise nothing
intro.body:
There are other front pieces — za-, po-, prze- and more. They make no promise at all: there is no reliable meaning to read off them, so do not try.

When you meet a verb with one of those on the front, treat it as a brand-new word and learn it whole, exactly the way you learned zrobić and wypić.

match.en: to go out, to leave (on foot)
to leave, to go away (by vehicle)
to get all the way there (on foot)
to get all the way there (by vehicle)
I got all the way there (m)

quiz.prompt: Tata ___ z domu o ósmej. (went out of the house)
quiz.explain: z domu is out of the house, and wy- is the front piece that says out.

quiz.prompt: Mama ___ do domu o szóstej. (came home, on foot)
quiz.explain: Coming towards home is przy-, not wy-; and on foot is the szedł verb, not the jechać one.

quiz.prompt: W końcu ___ do sklepu. (I finally got all the way there, m)
quiz.explain: do- is the reaching one — it is about getting all the way to the place, which is exactly what w końcu is telling you.

quiz.prompt: Zawsze ___ książkę. (I give the book back)
quiz.explain: Giving something back is od- — away from me, back to the person it came from.

quiz.prompt: departure — ___ (the word on the station board)
quiz.explain: od- is the away one, so odjazd is the leaving. przyjazd, with przy- on the front, is its opposite: the arrival.
Leaving is wy-, and a car makes it the jechać verb rather than the on-foot one.

choices: I got all the way to the pharmacy
I went out of the pharmacy
I go to the pharmacy every day
I gave it back to the pharmacy
quiz.answer: I got all the way to the pharmacy
quiz.explain: do- says the journey finished at the place. The pharmacy is where I ended up, not where I started.

choices: I went out of the office
I reached the office at last
quiz.answer: I went out of the office
quiz.explain: wy- plus z is out of — the office is what I left, not what I arrived at.

choices: My brother goes by bus every day
My brother gave the bus back
quiz.explain: przy- is the arriving one. If he had been leaving it would have been wyjechał.

quiz.prompt: Przyjazd o ósmej. — what does the board say?
quiz.explain: przy- toward, od- away: przyjazd is the arrival and odjazd is the departure.

choices: I reach the book at last
quiz.explain: od- is the away-and-back one. The book goes back to whoever it came from.
